security_audit.summary: All 65 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, normal Python imports, example URLs, endpoint-only environment access, and troubleshooting text. Two contextual risks remain: copy-ready examples use mutable latest image tags, and an unguarded example deletes a cloud agent version. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Creation examples deploy container images with the mutable latest tag.
remediation.suggestion: Use immutable image digests or fixed version tags in every deployment example.

remediation.issue: The deletion example removes an agent version without target validation or confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: List versions, verify the exact target, and require explicit confirmation before deletion.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Container Image Tags in Creation Examples
semantic_findings.description: Copy-ready creation examples use the latest tag, so a moved registry tag can change which container code Azure executes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both executable examples explicitly reference latest, although the later best-practice section advises fixed production tags.

semantic_findings.title: Cloud Agent Version Deletion Without a Guard
semantic_findings.description: The example directly deletes an Azure agent version without validating the target or requiring confirmation, creating accidental resource-loss risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The delete_version call is explicit and unguarded, but it targets a named version and is presented as an intentional management operation.

content.user_title: Build Container-Based Azure AI Hosted Agents
content.value_statement: Deploying custom agent containers in Azure AI Foundry requires precise SDK, identity, registry, and protocol configuration. This skill provides focused Python patterns for creating and managing hosted agents.
actual_capabilities: Configures AIProjectClient with DefaultAzureCredential and a project endpoint.
Creates versioned hosted agents from Azure Container Registry images.
Defines response protocol, CPU, memory, tools, and container environment variables.
Lists and deletes hosted agent versions with the Python SDK.
Provides synchronous and asynchronous agent creation patterns.
Explains common image, permission, capability host, and protocol errors.
limitations: Requires an existing Azure AI project, container registry, capability host, and assigned pull permissions.
Does not build, scan, or publish the container image.
Does not provision Azure resources or role assignments.
Examples require validation against the installed preview SDK and current Azure service limits.

use_cases.title: Create a First Hosted Agent
use_cases.description: Prepare a Python workflow that authenticates and deploys a custom container as an Azure AI hosted agent.

use_cases.title: Standardize Deployment Configuration
use_cases.description: Define consistent protocols, resources, tools, image references, and environment settings for hosted agent releases.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Hosted Agent Failures
use_cases.description: Review registry permissions, image paths, capability hosts, and protocol versions when agent creation fails.

prompt_templates.title: Check Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure AI project setup for a container-based hosted agent. Identify missing SDK, registry, identity, capability host, and endpoint requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Agent Creation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Python hosted-agent workflow for image [image reference], agent [name], CPU [value], and memory [value]. Use DefaultAzureCredential and fixed image tags.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Tools and Runtime
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my hosted-agent design with [tools], protocol [protocol], and these non-secret environment settings: [settings]. Explain required permissions and trust boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Azure hosted-agent deployment plan: [plan]. Check image immutability, least privilege, secret handling, MCP trust, resource sizing, cleanup controls, and async lifecycle management.

output_examples.input: Plan a hosted agent named invoice-reader using a fixed registry image and modest resources.
output_examples.output: A deployment outline with prerequisite checks, authenticated client setup, a versioned image reference, response protocol configuration, one CPU, and two GiB memory.

output_examples.input: Explain why my hosted agent reports ImagePullBackOff.
output: Confirm that the image path and fixed tag exist in the registry.
Verify that the project managed identity has the AcrPull role.
Check registry networking and retry after permission propagation.

output_examples.output: An async lifecycle plan that opens credential and project client contexts, creates one agent version, reports its state, and closes both clients.

best_practices: Use immutable image digests or fixed version tags for repeatable deployments.
Grant only required registry and project permissions through managed identities.
Validate tool endpoints, protect secrets, and confirm destructive operations before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy production agents from mutable latest image tags.
Do not place credentials or secrets directly in source code or container settings.
Do not enable code execution, file access, or MCP tools without reviewing their trust boundaries.

faq.question: Which Python packages are required?
faq.answer: The examples use azure-ai-projects version 2.0.0b3 or later and azure-identity.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: The skill uses DefaultAzureCredential, which can select supported local or managed Azure identities.

faq.question: Must the container image be in Azure Container Registry?
faq.answer: The documented workflow assumes Azure Container Registry and requires the project managed identity to have pull access.

faq.question: Can I configure tools for the hosted agent?
faq.answer: Yes. Examples cover code interpreter, file search, and MCP tools, but each tool requires a security review.

faq.question: Does the skill support asynchronous Python?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an async pattern using Azure credential and project client context managers.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It documents hosted-agent SDK operations and assumes the required Azure resources and permissions already exist.
